evidence.V1: Reads as a flower from front, three-quarter, top (six-petal rosette with gold centre) and silhouette.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: bloom head (big), stem and two leaves (medium), domed gold centre (small).
evidence.V3: Bloom size is pleasingly exaggerated, but the stem is a perfectly straight uniform tube and the leaves are flat cards; partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Petals have hard faceted bevels while leaves are razor-thin cards with sharp tips; edge treatment is inconsistent across parts.
evidence.V5: Bloom close-ups (studio and flat) show jagged, stepped edges where petals interpenetrate (right side of the head) and stray hard facets across petal tops; minor.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one petal hue in 2-3 values, leaf-green secondary, gold centre; bluebell and sunset colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V7: 560 tris vs small target 600, under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and kit palette, but organic parts are separate shells (petals overlapping, leaves stuck on the stem base) rather than the kit's fused smooth shells.
evidence.V9: Foliage studio line correct (anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery off, white colour, origin bottom-centre); seats pass with no gaps.

artifacts: jagged stepped edges where petals overlap/interpenetrate (bloom close-up, right side)
stray hard facets across petal surfaces
leaves are paper-thin cards with the left leaf tucked behind the stem base
top_fixes: Smooth/fuse the petal ring so overlaps do not create zig-zag edges and petals shade softly
Give the stem a gentle curve and taper and thicken/curl the leaves so they read as fused organic forms
Add a slight root flare or small ground tuft at the stem base so it seats naturally
